search_notes: The NHRA file is empty (nhra=false throughout). The session web-search cap was reached part way through, so the work rests on pages already downloaded. Sources: Consumer Guide 911 History (HowStuffWorks, Wayback copy; the live site is behind a bot wall); the Excellence magazine specs database (a US magazine covering US-spec cars, mostly DIN figures); Wikipedia (classic/930/964/993 articles and List of Porsche engines with US engine type numbers, counted as one source); EPA 1984+ (size, cylinders and turbo only; no 1985 rows). The Porsche AG 60-years press kit and the archived PCNA Porsche Classic pages quote European/German DIN figures only, so they back displacement and model existence but not US ratings. Hagerty valuation tools need a login; Total 911 datafiles now redirect to futureplc; auction listings were ignored. Rating rule: hp = the US SAE figure when 2+ sources state it, or when Consumer Guide's SAE figure matches the 2+-source DIN figure after conversion (PS x 0.9863). Otherwise hp = the US-spec DIN figure that 2+ sources agree on, hp_basis says DIN, and Consumer Guide's SAE figure goes in hp_sae_us_consumer_guide and the note. v2 (2026-10-14): US SAE ratings firmed up from the Standard Catalog of Imported Cars (Krause) and Leffingwell's Porsche 911 Buyer's Guide via Internet Archive full-text search snippets, plus Porsche factory/US brochures (Internet Archive scans, Stuttcars PDF scans) and the Der Whites literature catalogue. All Porsche literature counts as one source. Rows whose v1 hp was DIN keep that figure in hp_din_us_spec.
